findings.issue_text: [BUG] The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but message_builder only receives unsubscribe_url when explicitly passed, so every other notification email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true hits a missing-interpolation error at I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args). All non-topic notification emails (PMs, invites, any builder caller that does not pass unsubscribe_url) raise I18n::MissingInterpolationData when the unsubscribe link is rendered, so email delivery for those paths breaks entirely, not just gains a new link.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls current_user.id and tu.notification_level without nil guards: anonymous visitors (the email link is a plain GET with check_xhr skipped) and users with no existing TopicUser record both crash. An anonymous user clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link in an email gets a 500 NoMethodError on nil instead of a login redirect; a logged-in user who never opened the topic (no topic_users row) gets `tu.notification_level` NoMethodError → 500 instead of unsubscribing.

[BUG] The route name topicUnsubscribe resolves to template 'topic-unsubscribe' under Ember's resolver, but the diff places the template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs (name 'topic/unsubscribe'), so the route cannot find its template. Navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe client-side renders a missing-template error/blank page instead of the unsubscribe UI; the hbs file as located is unreachable by the declared route name.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled 'stopNotificiationsText' (Notificiations) and is consumed by the template under the same misspelling. Works today only because the typo is mirrored in the template; any future contributor referencing the natural spelling ('stopNotificationsText') binds to undefined and silently renders an empty paragraph.

[ADVISORY] The slug-mismatch redirect uses TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user) before any authentication/permission check and then redirects to topic.unsubscribe_url, but for the slugless route 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe' params[:slug] is nil so slugs_do_not_match forces a 301 on every request to that route. The slugless unsubscribe route can never execute its unsubscribe logic — it always redirects to the slugful URL — so the route definition for 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe' is dead code and adds an extra redirect hop for clients that emit the id-only form.

[BUG] unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError (500) for any logged-in user who has no existing TopicUser record, because TopicUser.find_by returns nil and the code immediately calls tu.notification_level A user clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link in an email before ever having visited/interacted with the topic (TopicUser row only created by TopicUser.change/track_visit!), and gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed — the primary happy path of the feature fails

[BUG] unsubscribe calls current_user.id with no anonymous-user guard, so an anonymous visitor hits NoMethodError on nil and gets a 500 The route is a plain GET skipped from check_xhr and reachable by anyone; anyone not logged in (or whose session expired, e.g. clicking an old email link) gets a server error page instead of a login prompt or the unsubscribe page

[BUG] unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes that template arg — every other email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument because the key is absent from template_args Any mailer path that opts into the unsubscribe link without an unsubscribe_url (the sibling flag on the same touched notification path that was not enumerated) fails to render the email and errors out at send time — sibling-flag-propagation miss: other send_notification_email-adjacent callers and other notification email types were not updated

[BUG] the topicUnsubscribe route is declared after the topic resource whose nested fromParamsNear route ('/:nearPost') already matches /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, so the Ember route is shadowed and unreachable Clicking the email link boots Ember, which matches the existing topic route with nearPost='unsubscribe' and renders the topic page instead of the unsubscribe page (or errors trying to interpret 'unsubscribe' as a post number), defeating the feature for client-side navigation

[BUG] unsubscribe is a GET request that mutates user state (TopicUser#save!), so email-client link prefetchers and security scanners silently unsubscribe/mute users who never clicked Users on clients that prefetch links (Outlook, some webmail) get their notification level changed to regular/muted without any user intent; the change is also invisible because it happens from an email, not the app

[BUG] the else branch sets notification_level to muted for users already at regular or below, so 'stop notifications for this topic' silently mutes the topic rather than only downgrading tracking/watching A user at regular level who clicks the link in an email worded as 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' gets the topic fully muted (a stronger state the email never promised), with no confirmation of what actually happened

[ADVISORY] no test in the diff covers the new unsubscribe controller action (the only touched spec is message_builder_spec, which asserts the List-Unsubscribe header only); the nil-TopicUser, anonymous-user, slug-mismatch-redirect, and toggle-level paths are all unverified The exact failure modes above (nil tu 500, anon 500, mute-instead-of-unsubscribe) would have been caught by even one controller spec; regressions in this endpoint ship silently

[ADVISORY] computed property and locale-derived label are named 'stopNotificiationsText' (misspelled 'Notifications'), a typo baked into a new public-ish controller property Future greps/refactors for 'notifications' miss this property, and anyone extending the unsubscribe page copies the misspelling further; caught now it costs one rename, later it spreads

[ADVISORY] perform_show_response now contains an unconditional render :show in the html branch, changing behavior for every caller of this shared helper, not just unsubscribe The next action that calls perform_show_response in an html context where it previously relied on implicit rendering now gets an explicit show-template render (or a DoubleRenderError if it renders itself), a hidden coupling added by this diff

[BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by and immediately dereferences tu.notification_level with no nil check, so any user without an existing topic_users row (or an anonymous/logged-out visitor hitting the skip_xhr GET route) crashes with NoMethodError on nil. The unsubscribe link in emails is sent to users precisely because they may not have visited the topic recently, but users whose TopicUser record was never created get a 500 instead of being unsubscribed; anonymous clicks get a 500.

[BUG] The rewritten unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url; every other mailer path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g. digest and PM emails built via Email::MessageBuilder) does not supply it, so I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') raises I18n::MissingInterpolationValue. Email sending for any notification type other than post notifications crashes (or renders a broken 'missing translation' string), silently dropping mail for users — under-scoping: the new template argument was only wired through one of the consumers of the shared template.

[BUG] The diff drops the post_number: /\d+/ constraint from both summary routes while rewriting them, changing route matching semantics as an untraceable side effect of adding the unsubscribe routes. URLs like /t/slug/123/summary/abc that previously 404ed now match topics#show, and the route ordering swap changes which pattern wins for edge inputs — behavior change with no requirement behind it.

[BUG] The GET unsubscribe action performs a state-changing write (TopicUser notification_level toggle) with no CSRF protection and no confirmation, on a route skipped from check_xhr. Email scanners and link prefetchers that follow links will mute/track the topic for the user without any intent, flipping notification levels as a side effect of a GET — an invariant (GET is safe/idempotent, notification changes are user-initiated) this design does not enforce.

[ADVISORY] The toggle semantics silently change tracking/watching users to muted on first click, not to 'regular', and there is no state check distinguishing watched/tracked/regular — a user with :watching loses watch-level emails via the same link. Users subscribed at watch level who click 'stop notifications for this topic' are dropped all the way to muted (or worse, a second click mutes a regular user), which does not match the email copy 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic'.

[ADVISORY] Computed property is named stopNotificiationsText (typo: 'Notificiations') and is referenced by the template, baking the misspelling into both sides of a hand-maintained name pair. The next editor searching for 'notifications' fails to find the property, and renaming one side without the other yields a silent blank paragraph; also the property outputs raw HTML consumed via triple-stash {{{}}}, coupling i18n strings to HTML trust.

[ADVISORY] The title-emptiness guard added to dropdown-button's renderString is unrelated behavioral work smuggled into the unsubscribe feature — no requirement in this PR concerns dropdown titles. Scope drift: reviewers and bisects attribute a shared-component rendering change to the email feature; if any existing dropdown relied on rendering an empty <h4> for spacing, its layout changes silently.

[ADVISORY] Roughly half of the topic_user.rb diff is pure reformatting (scope indentation, create_lookup one-lining, MessageBus publish spacing, where-hash syntax) with zero behavioral trace to the unsubscribe requirement. The change-hiding risk of cosmetic churn: a future revert or blame on notification-level logic now routes through this feature commit, and any accidental semantic change in the reformatted lines is invisible in review.

[ADVISORY] The notification email template diff is almost entirely whitespace/reindentation churn around the two functional lines (adding the unsubscribe_link footer block), obscuring the actual change. Reviewers must mentally diff the reindentation to spot the one functional addition; a semantic break inside the moved blocks (e.g. the duplicated %{respond_instructions} footer now appearing both inside and outside the context_posts conditional, as it did before) would be missed — and indeed the structure now renders respond_instructions twice when context_posts is present.

[ADVISORY] The full-body rewrite of topic-from-params.js.es6 (var→const, function→shorthand, reordering declarations) is unrelated style churn inside a feature PR about unsubscribe. The only functional delta in this file is a blank line; everything else is diff noise that inflates review surface and masks regressions in the topic-loading path.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe controller action — including the nil-TopicUser edge, the level-toggle logic, the slug-mismatch redirect, and the anonymous-user path — has no test anywhere in this diff; only message_builder's unsubscribe_url arg is covered. The core permission/state behavior of the feature is unguarded: a regression that, say, mutes the wrong user or 500s on missing TopicUser would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe_url is passed unconditionally as post.topic.unsubscribe_url even for notification types where post/topic context differs (e.g. PMs or group mentions), and the shared unsubscribe_link copy is shown to all recipients regardless of whether per-topic unsubscribe is meaningful. Users receive a 'stop notifications about this topic' link on emails (such as PMs) where the link's mute/unmute toggle is not the right semantic, training users to distrust the unsubscribe footer.

[ADVISORY] html_part substitutes %{unsubscribe_link} but the plain-text part of the same email is not handled in this diff, so the new per-topic unsubscribe link only exists in HTML emails. Text-only email clients show the old preferences-only unsubscribe copy (or a missing-interpolation artifact if the text template also consumes unsubscribe_link), an inconsistency between formats the diff does not address.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by without handling nil, so a user with no existing TopicUser row (never visited/tracked the topic) hits tu.notification_level on nil and gets a 500 NoMethodError instead of the unsubscribe the link promises. Email recipients who click the per-topic unsubscribe link before ever opening the topic receive a server error; the notification level is never changed, so they keep receiving emails for that topic — the feature's core promise fails for exactly the audience the link targets.

[BUG] unsubscribe performs a state-mutating write (TopicUser#save!) on a GET request that skips check_xhr, with no CSRF token and no guard against nil current_user. Any logged-out user hitting the URL gets a NoMethodError on current_user.id (500), and — worse — corporate email scanners and link prefetchers that follow GET links will silently toggle/mute notification levels for real users who never clicked anything, and the toggle semantics mean a scanner plus a real click can mute then re-enable unpredictably.

[BUG] The server.en.yml unsubscribe_link string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but message_builder only interpolates @template_args, so every caller with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not pass unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Any email path that enables the unsubscribe link without supplying the new argument (the only caller updated is send_notification_email) fails to render at all, turning previously-working notification emails into hard errors.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe_url builds a relative path ("#{url}/unsubscribe" where Topic#url is a relative /t/... URL) and it is used both in the email body and as the List-Unsubscribe header value, which requires an absolute https:// URL. Mail clients render a relative link that cannot resolve (broken or resolved against the webmail origin), and list-unsubscribe processors that honor the header reject or ignore a non-absolute URL, so one-click unsubscribe outside the mail body does not work.

[ADVISORY] The toggle semantics (level > regular ? regular : muted) conflate 'unsubscribe from this email' with a state machine that flips between muted and regular on every GET, with no authorization-level check that the user may read the topic. A user who had set 'watching' and clicks the email link is silently downgraded to 'regular' rather than muted (still emailed for replies-to-watched in some flows), and a repeat click re-enables notifications, making the link's promise ('You will stop receiving notifications') false; private/restricted topics are also probed via TopicView before any permission story is explicit.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is named stopNotificiationsText (misspelled 'Notificiations') while the template and locale key use the correct spelling, creating a confusable pair that will trip the next editor. Anyone adding a second reference (test, second template, refactoring rename) will half-rename and get an undefined property rendering empty text; the typo is already duplicated between property name and consumption site, so it is now load-bearing.

[ADVISORY] The t/:slug/:topic_id/summary route silently dropped its post_number: /\d+/ constraint in this diff, an unrelated behavior change riding along with the unsubscribe feature. Paths that previously failed to match the summary route (non-numeric third segment, e.g. /t/slug/123/xyz/summary shapes matching differently) now route to topics#show with an unconstrained :post_number param, changing URL matching for existing callers who relied on the old constraint.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by and immediately dereferences tu.notification_level, crashing with NoMethodError (500) for any user who has no topic_users row for the topic. The very users the per-topic unsubscribe email targets — recipients who never opened the topic and thus have no TopicUser record — click the email link and get a 500 instead of unsubscribing; the feature fails exactly on its primary audience.

[BUG] The rewritten unsubscribe_link locale string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder#html_part interpolates it for every message with add_unsubscribe_link while only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url, so all other unsub-linked emails raise I18n::MissingInterpolationError. Any notification path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without a per-topic URL (e.g. other notification senders, digests, summary emails that reuse the same builder path) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationError at render time, silently dropping or 500ing email delivery for flows the diff never touched — the feature's scope leaked into every emailed message.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action implements a toggle (regular-or-below becomes muted, above becomes regular) rather than the one-way 'stop notifications' the email link promises, so clicking the unsubscribe link in an old email re-subscribes a user who has since muted or lowered the topic. A user who unsubscribed and later re-muted gets silently flipped back to a higher notification level by re-clicking the link still sitting in their mailbox; the action's observable behavior (mute/re-subscribe toggle) diverges from the stated intent ('You will stop receiving notifications') which the confirmation page prints unconditionally in both directions.

[ADVISORY] The route diff silently rewrites the existing /t/:slug/:topic_id/summary constraint (drops post_number: /\d+/) and reorders moderator-liked/wordpress routes — route-definition changes unrelated to the unsubscribe feature bundled into this PR without acknowledgment. Reviewers and future readers cannot tell whether the summary-route constraint change was intentional; a behavior-affecting route edit rides in hidden inside a feature PR, and any regression there gets attributed to the wrong change during bisection.

[ADVISORY] The action skips check_xhr and performs a state mutation (notification_level change) on a plain GET request with no CSRF token or confirmation, changing the accepted constraint that state-changing topic operations go through XHR/PUT endpoints. Email scanners and link prefetchers that follow URLs in mail can toggle the recipient's notification level without the user ever seeing the page — an unsolicited side effect introduced by making a mutation a GET-navigable URL; next change to this action (e.g. adding analytics or double-render guards) inherits this coupling.

[ADVISORY] The only test coverage added for the unsubscribe_url plumbing is the happy path where the argument is supplied; the new non-trivial branches (missing unsubscribe_url with add_unsubscribe_link, and the controller's nil-TopicUser toggle logic) have no test in this diff. A regression in either the interpolation fallback or the toggle direction would pass CI; the uncovered behaviors are exactly the two failure modes that affect users (missing-interpolation errors and silent re-subscribe), so any future refactor of message_builder or the controller lands unguarded.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a state-changing notification-level update on a GET request with check_xhr skipped, and it dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser record. Two concrete failures: (1) any third-party page can embed an or a plain link and silently mute/change the notification level of any logged-in visitor's topics — the endpoint mutates state on GET with no CSRF token and no XHR check; (2) when the current user has no TopicUser row for the topic (never tracked/visited it), TopicUser.find_by returns nil and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError, yielding a 500 instead of a graceful response.

[ADVISORY] The template uses the triple-stash {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} to render a string built by interpolating the user-controlled topic title into an i18n message containing raw <strong> markup. XSS safety of this page hinges entirely on the server-side pre-escaping of fancy_title; the triple-stash bypasses Ember's escaping, so any future change to how the title is computed/transported (e.g. a raw title field) turns this page into a stored-XSS vector. The author's rebuttal — 'fancy_title is already entity-escaped' — survives today, but the escaping invariant is now load-bearing in a template that looks like free-form HTML output.

[ADVISORY] The slug-mismatch redirect uses HTTP 301 (permanent) for what is a canonicalization convenience redirect. Browsers and intermediaries permanently cache the 301 mapping of the wrong-slug URL to the canonical unsubscribe URL; if a topic's slug later changes or the route is removed, users are stuck hitting a cached redirect to a dead endpoint, and the permanently-cached response can also be replayed cross-user by shared caches on the non-XHR GET path.

[BUG] The new unsubscribe_url option is passed into the builder but no assertion verifies it is used — the spec only re-runs the pre-existing List-Unsubscribe header presence check, so the new topic-specific unsubscribe feature is exercised by a test that passes regardless of whether the URL ever reaches the email. The message builder's html_part interpolates %{unsubscribe_link} via I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args); if template_args silently failed to include unsubscribe_url (or a future refactor dropped it from @opts), this spec still passes and users' per-topic unsubscribe links silently regress to the generic preferences link, which is the exact behavior this PR exists to ship.

[ADVISORY] The entire unsubscribe action — the notification_level toggle (regular→muted else muted→regular), the slug-mismatch redirect, and the skip_before_filter/check_xhr change — has no test coverage; the only test-shaped file in this diff (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) references nothing from TopicsController, TopicUser, or the /unsubscribe route. A regression in the toggle direction (e.g. a user who is already muted being bumped to 'regular' and re-subscribed to notifications by clicking 'unsubscribe') would not be caught by any spec; the toggle is inverted-susceptible logic (an if/else over notification level) and its only behavioral guard is this PR shipping it uncovered.

[BUG] unsubscribe looks up TopicUser with find_by and immediately dereferences tu.notification_level, so any user who has no topic_users row (never visited/never notified for that topic) crashes with NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a graceful response. A recipient clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link in an email for a topic where TopicUser row does not exist (e.g. row pruned, or notification created before tracking row) gets a 500 error and cannot unsubscribe; no data is written.

[BUG] check_xhr is skipped for :unsubscribe but the action calls current_user.id with no signed-in guard, so an anonymous request crashes with NoMethodError on nil.id (500) instead of redirecting to login. Any unauthenticated hit to /t/:id/unsubscribe (e.g. email client link prefetcher) produces a 500; repeated email-link prefetching spam the error logs.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a destructive, irreversible state change (overwrites notification_level) on a GET request with no confirmation and no CSRF protection (check_xhr skipped), and the toggle logic silently destroys the user's prior level: a 'watching' user clicking the link is demoted only to :regular (still emailed), while the level they had is lost with no record. Email link prefetchers or accidental clicks permanently overwrite the user's notification_level with no audit trail or undo; watching users who click 'stop notifications' keep getting emails because the branch sets :regular instead of :muted.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe_url is only passed for send_notification_email; other notification mailer paths (e.g. PM/invite-style builders) that share the %{unsubscribe_link} template now interpolate an empty %{unsubscribe_url} template arg, producing a broken '(click here)()' link. Every email template that renders the updated unsubscribe_link locale string but does not set opts[:unsubscribe_url] ships a dead link to users.

[ADVISORY] TopicView.new is constructed and a full topic_view serialization is performed on every unsubscribe hit before the TopicUser mutation, an unconditional heavy read+render on a route now reachable without XHR headers. Prefetching email clients hitting /t/:id/unsubscribe trigger full TopicView loads (topic, posts, permissions) per click, adding DB load for a page whose only purpose is a state toggle.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil for users with no TopicUser row, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the GET /t/:id/unsubscribe link in emails 500s instead of unsubscribing or returning a 4xx. Any user who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link before ever having a topic_users row (or for a deleted/invalid topic_id) gets a raw 500; the unsubscribe silently does not happen.

[BUG] The toggle logic only demotes levels above :regular down to :regular, so a tracking/watching user who clicks 'stop notifications' is left at :regular and keeps receiving notification emails while the operation reports success. The email says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here'; a tracking user clicks, gets a success page, and continues to be emailed — silently partial success.

[BUG] The Ember topic-unsubscribe route never calls the unsubscribe endpoint or changes notification_level; it renders a page whose text claims 'You will stop receiving notifications' while performing no state change. Any client path that lands on /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (Ember transition, XHR navigation) shows the success message without unsubscribing — the UI reports success while dropping the work.

[BUG] The unsubscribe_link template now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url; every other builder with add_unsubscribe_link renders a 'click here' link with an empty href. All non-notification emails that include the unsubscribe footer (e.g., digest/summary paths reaching html_part with add_unsubscribe_link) ship a dead link, misdirecting users trying to unsubscribe.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe performs a state-changing save on a GET request with no POST/confirmation step. Link prefetchers, email scanners, and previews fire the GET and silently mutate the user's notification level; the user's subscription is changed without intent. (Overlap with Security for CSRF, flagged here for the silent-mutation reliability angle.)

[ADVISORY] PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id) has no rejection handler, so a failed topic load leaves the route in the generic Ember error state with the email-promised unsubscribe page never rendered. A transient load failure converts the one-shot unsubscribe link click into an unexplained error page with no retry guidance.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe routes are not constrained to numeric topic_id on the slug variant consistently and the :summary route lost its post_number constraint in this reorder, changing match behavior for URLs like /t/slug/1/summary. Previously-rejected URLs now match :summary with post_number as part of topic_id constraints, silently rerouting malformed links.

adjudication.rationale: The router map adds a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe` (`this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });`). Ember resolves that route name to the dasherized template/controller/view names (i.e., `topic-unsubscribe`). The diff adds `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, and `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, matching that expectation, but the template is added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which would be resolved as `topic/unsubscribe` (nested under a `topic` resource) rather than `topic-unsubscribe`. With only what’s shown in the diff, this route would not find its template and would render the missing template/blank output.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the guard `(!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` will always be true for the slugless HTML route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, causing an unconditional 301 redirect to `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` before the notification-level update runs. adjudication.rationale: While the diff does remove `post_number: /\d+/` from the Rails route constraint for `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/summary" => "topics#show"` (it changes from `constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/, post_number: /\d+/}` to `constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/}`), the route path itself contains no `:post_number` segment at all. Therefore URLs like `/t/slug/123/xyz/summary` still will not match this route because of the extra `/xyz` segment, regardless of any `post_number` constraint. The finding’s claim about changing matching for a non-numeric third segment is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by and immediately dereferences tu.notification_level, crashing with NoMethodError (500) for any user who has no topic_users row for the topic. The very users the per-topic unsubscribe email targets — recipients who never opened the topic and thus have no TopicUser record — click the email link and get a 500 instead of unsubscribing; the feature fails exactly on its primary audience.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level`. If `find_by` returns `nil` (no `topic_users` row for that user/topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. The diff does not include any guard or creation of a TopicUser record in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten unsubscribe_link locale string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder#html_part interpolates it for every message with add_unsubscribe_link while only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url, so all other unsub-linked emails raise I18n::MissingInterpolationError. Any notification path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without a per-topic URL (e.g. other notification senders, digests, summary emails that reuse the same builder path) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationError at render time, silently dropping or 500ing email delivery for flows the diff never touched — the feature's scope leaked into every emailed message.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/locales/server.en.yml`, `unsubscribe_link` was changed to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, and `template_args` only includes `unsubscribe_url` if the caller passed it via opts. The diff only adds `unsubscribe_url` in `UserNotifications#send_notification_email`, and the spec update (`message_builder_spec`) also had to start passing `unsubscribe_url`, indicating this interpolation is now required. Therefore any other email path that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but doesn't supply `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationError` at render time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action implements a toggle (regular-or-below becomes muted, above becomes regular) rather than the one-way 'stop notifications' the email link promises, so clicking the unsubscribe link in an old email re-subscribes a user who has since muted or lowered the topic. A user who unsubscribed and later re-muted gets silently flipped back to a higher notification level by re-clicking the link still sitting in their mailbox; the action's observable behavior (mute/re-subscribe toggle) diverges from the stated intent ('You will stop receiving notifications') which the confirmation page prints unconditionally in both directions.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the notification level is only ever reduced: if `tu.notification_level > regular` it is set to `regular`, otherwise it is set to `muted`. There is no path that increases a user from `muted` (or any level `<= regular`) back to a higher level, so re-clicking an old link cannot “re-subscribe” someone who has muted/lowered the topic. While the action does branch between `regular` and `muted`, the specific claimed buggy behavior (mute/re-subscribe toggle that can flip a muted user back up) is not supported by the diff.

Reviewers and future readers cannot tell whether the summary-route constraint change was intentional; a behavior-affecting route edit rides in hidden inside a feature PR, and any regression there gets attributed to the wrong change during bisection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in config/routes.rb does remove the `post_number: /\d+/` constraint from both summary routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/summary"` and `get "t/:topic_id/summary"`) and reorders the `moderator-liked` and `wordpress` routes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The action skips check_xhr and performs a state mutation (notification_level change) on a plain GET request with no CSRF token or confirmation, changing the accepted constraint that state-changing topic operations go through XHR/PUT endpoints. Email scanners and link prefetchers that follow URLs in mail can toggle the recipient's notification level without the user ever seeing the page — an unsolicited side effect introduced by making a mutation a GET-navigable URL; next change to this action (e.g. adding analytics or double-render guards) inherits this coupling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that is reachable via GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and explicitly skips the XHR check (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). That action mutates state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` based solely on visiting the URL. Since it is a GET endpoint, it will not have Rails’ CSRF protection semantics for non-idempotent operations, and the link is propagated into emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` + server locale `unsubscribe_link` includes `%{unsubscribe_url}`), making it susceptible to email client link prefetching/scanning triggering unintended notification level toggles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test coverage added for the unsubscribe_url plumbing is the happy path where the argument is supplied; the new non-trivial branches (missing unsubscribe_url with add_unsubscribe_link, and the controller's nil-TopicUser toggle logic) have no test in this diff. A regression in either the interpolation fallback or the toggle direction would pass CI; the uncovered behaviors are exactly the two failure modes that affect users (missing-interpolation errors and silent re-subscribe), so any future refactor of message_builder or the controller lands unguarded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new non-trivial behavior without corresponding coverage beyond a happy-path plumbing test. In `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`, the only new expectation is built around providing `unsubscribe_url`, while `lib/email/message_builder.rb` always interpolates `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true and the updated `config/locales/server.en.yml` string now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}`—there’s no test for the case where `add_unsubscribe_link: true` is set but `unsubscribe_url` is omitted (which could raise missing interpolation). Separately, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` introduces branching toggle logic on `tu.notification_level` after `TopicUser.find_by(...)` with no spec added for edge cases (including `tu` being nil), so regressions in that new controller behavior would not be caught by tests shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a state-changing notification-level update on a GET request with check_xhr skipped, and it dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser record. Two concrete failures: (1) any third-party page can embed an or a plain link and silently mute/change the notification level of any logged-in visitor's topics — the endpoint mutates state on GET with no CSRF token and no XHR check; (2) when the current user has no TopicUser row for the topic (never tracked/visited it), TopicUser.find_by returns nil and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError, yielding a 500 instead of a graceful response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `GET` endpoint `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) that mutates state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). The controller also explicitly skips the `check_xhr` filter for `:unsubscribe`, making it callable via normal browser requests. Because this is a state-changing action on GET, it is CSRF-prone (e.g., an embedded image/link can trigger it for a logged-in user). Additionally, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return `nil`, and the subsequent `tu.notification_level` dereference will raise, causing a 500 when no TopicUser row exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The template uses the triple-stash {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} to render a string built by interpolating the user-controlled topic title into an i18n message containing raw <strong> markup. XSS safety of this page hinges entirely on the server-side pre-escaping of fancy_title; the triple-stash bypasses Ember's escaping, so any future change to how the title is computed/transported (e.g. a raw title field) turns this page into a stored-XSS vector. The author's rebuttal — 'fancy_title is already entity-escaped' — survives today, but the escaping invariant is now load-bearing in a template that looks like free-form HTML output.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` rendering `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stash), which bypasses Ember/Handlebars escaping. That string is produced in the new controller `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the new client locale `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` embeds HTML (`{{title}}`). Since topic titles are user-controlled in general, this change can render title-derived content as raw HTML on the page, creating an XSS risk unless `model.fancyTitle` is guaranteed to be entity-escaped everywhere (not verifiable from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The slug-mismatch redirect uses HTTP 301 (permanent) for what is a canonicalization convenience redirect. Browsers and intermediaries permanently cache the 301 mapping of the wrong-slug URL to the canonical unsubscribe URL; if a topic's slug later changes or the route is removed, users are stuck hitting a cached redirect to a dead endpoint, and the permanently-cached response can also be replayed cross-user by shared caches on the non-XHR GET path.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, slug mismatch (or missing slug on non-JSON) triggers `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. The diff clearly introduces/uses a permanent redirect for what appears to be a canonicalization redirect similar to other topic routes. The concern about long-lived caching of a 301 mapping is a reasonable, specific review issue grounded in this code, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior or a security defect in practice (it’s largely an HTTP semantics/caching policy choice).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new unsubscribe_url option is passed into the builder but no assertion verifies it is used — the spec only re-runs the pre-existing List-Unsubscribe header presence check, so the new topic-specific unsubscribe feature is exercised by a test that passes regardless of whether the URL ever reaches the email. The message builder's html_part interpolates %{unsubscribe_link} via I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args); if template_args silently failed to include unsubscribe_url (or a future refactor dropped it from @opts), this spec still passes and users' per-topic unsubscribe links silently regress to the generic preferences link, which is the exact behavior this PR exists to ship.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb the new argument `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` is added when constructing `Email::MessageBuilder`, but the shown test still only asserts the pre-existing behavior: `List-Unsubscribe` header presence. Nothing in the diff adds an assertion that the topic-specific unsubscribe URL is actually interpolated into the cooked `%{unsubscribe_link}` (which in lib/email/message_builder.rb comes from `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly introduced behavior, not a runtime defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire unsubscribe action — the notification_level toggle (regular→muted else muted→regular), the slug-mismatch redirect, and the skip_before_filter/check_xhr change — has no test coverage; the only test-shaped file in this diff (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) references nothing from TopicsController, TopicUser, or the /unsubscribe route. A regression in the toggle direction (e.g. a user who is already muted being bumped to 'regular' and re-subscribed to notifications by clicking 'unsubscribe') would not be caught by any spec; the toggle is inverted-susceptible logic (an if/else over notification level) and its only behavioral guard is this PR shipping it uncovered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (including slug-mismatch redirect, `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` expansion, and notification level toggle logic on `TopicUser`) plus new routes (`/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) and Ember route/template wiring. The only spec change shown is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`, which tests email unsubscribe-link handling and does not exercise the new controller action, routes, or `TopicUser` notification toggle behavior. So the finding about missing test coverage for this newly introduced, behavior-heavy endpoint is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] unsubscribe looks up TopicUser with find_by and immediately dereferences tu.notification_level, so any user who has no topic_users row (never visited/never notified for that topic) crashes with NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a graceful response. A recipient clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link in an email for a topic where TopicUser row does not exist (e.g. row pruned, or notification created before tracking row) gets a 500 error and cannot unsubscribe; no data is written.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it via `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!`. If no `TopicUser` row exists, `tu` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response rather than gracefully handling the unsubscribe request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] check_xhr is skipped for :unsubscribe but the action calls current_user.id with no signed-in guard, so an anonymous request crashes with NoMethodError on nil.id (500) instead of redirecting to login. Any unauthenticated hit to /t/:id/unsubscribe (e.g. email client link prefetcher) produces a 500; repeated email-link prefetching spam the error logs.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` and implements `unsubscribe` using `current_user.id` (`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`) with no visible authentication/signed-in guard in the action itself. If `current_user` is nil, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.id`, producing a 500 on unauthenticated requests to the new `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a destructive, irreversible state change (overwrites notification_level) on a GET request with no confirmation and no CSRF protection (check_xhr skipped), and the toggle logic silently destroys the user's prior level: a 'watching' user clicking the link is demoted only to :regular (still emailed), while the level they had is lost with no record. Email link prefetchers or accidental clicks permanently overwrite the user's notification_level with no audit trail or undo; watching users who click 'stop notifications' keep getting emails because the branch sets :regular instead of :muted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe` as a **GET** route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) and explicitly skips `check_xhr` for it (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). That action mutates and persists state (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) with no confirmation and (because it’s GET) no CSRF protection by default. The toggle logic also overwrites the user’s prior notification level: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it is forced down to `:regular`, otherwise it is set to `:muted`, so a higher level (e.g., watching/tracking) is lost rather than being restored/recorded, and it doesn’t necessarily align with the “stop notifications” copy added in `client.en.yml`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] unsubscribe_url is only passed for send_notification_email; other notification mailer paths (e.g. PM/invite-style builders) that share the %{unsubscribe_link} template now interpolate an empty %{unsubscribe_url} template arg, producing a broken '(click here)()' link. Every email template that renders the updated unsubscribe_link locale string but does not set opts[:unsubscribe_url] ships a dead link to users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, and `template_args` only includes `user_preferences_url` by default (no default `unsubscribe_url`). Therefore any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` will now produce a broken interpolation (typically an I18n MissingInterpolationArgument error, or at best an empty link). The diff only shows `send_notification_email` being updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, so the risk is introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicView.new is constructed and a full topic_view serialization is performed on every unsubscribe hit before the TopicUser mutation, an unconditional heavy read+render on a route now reachable without XHR headers. Prefetching email clients hitting /t/:id/unsubscribe trigger full TopicView loads (topic, posts, permissions) per click, adding DB load for a page whose only purpose is a state toggle.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is constructed at the start of the request, and the action ends by calling `perform_show_response`, which (per diff) preloads `topic_view_serializer` and `render :show` for HTML. Additionally, `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` now includes `:unsubscribe`, making this reachable without XHR. While the exact DB “heaviness” of `TopicView.new` isn’t quantified in the diff, the control flow does unconditionally build a full TopicView and render the standard topic payload for an unsubscribe hit, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil for users with no TopicUser row, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the GET /t/:id/unsubscribe link in emails 500s instead of unsubscribing or returning a 4xx. Any user who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link before ever having a topic_users row (or for a deleted/invalid topic_id) gets a raw 500; the unsubscribe silently does not happen.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, assigns, and `tu.save!`) with no nil-check or fallback creation. Since `find_by` can return `nil` when no `topic_users` row exists, this will raise `NoMethodError` and cause a 500 on `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` for such users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The toggle logic only demotes levels above :regular down to :regular, so a tracking/watching user who clicks 'stop notifications' is left at :regular and keeps receiving notification emails while the operation reports success. The email says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here'; a tracking user clicks, gets a success page, and continues to be emailed — silently partial success.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the notification level is toggled as:

```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
```

So a user currently at `:tracking`/`:watching` (levels above `:regular`) is only demoted to `:regular`, not muted. Yet the new email copy (`server.en.yml`) and the unsubscribe page text (`client.en.yml` + `topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) both state "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" / "You will stop receiving notifications". The diff-grounded logic therefore does not guarantee “stop” for users above `:regular`—it performs only a partial reduction, contradicting the promised behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Ember topic-unsubscribe route never calls the unsubscribe endpoint or changes notification_level; it renders a page whose text claims 'You will stop receiving notifications' while performing no state change. Any client path that lands on /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (Ember transition, XHR navigation) shows the success message without unsubscribing — the UI reports success while dropping the work.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember `topic-unsubscribe` route (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`) only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and never issues a request to the new Rails `topics#unsubscribe` endpoint (`get ... => topics#unsubscribe`). Yet the template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) renders `stopNotificiationsText` which asserts the user will stop receiving notifications. Therefore, if the app transitions client-side to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (handled by the Ember router entry in `app-route-map.js.es6`), it will display the “stop receiving notifications” message without performing the server-side notification_level toggle in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe_link template now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url; every other builder with add_unsubscribe_link renders a 'click here' link with an empty href. All non-notification emails that include the unsubscribe footer (e.g., digest/summary paths reaching html_part with add_unsubscribe_link) ship a dead link, misdirecting users trying to unsubscribe.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is set. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` is updated here to pass `unsubscribe_url`, plus one spec. The diff does not show other callers of `Email::MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link`, so the claim about “every other builder”/digests shipping a dead link isn’t verifiable from this diff. However, the change does introduce a new required interpolation argument that other call sites may need to supply (or a fallback should be added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] unsubscribe performs a state-changing save on a GET request with no POST/confirmation step. Link prefetchers, email scanners, and previews fire the GET and silently mutate the user's notification level; the user's subscription is changed without intent. (Overlap with Security for CSRF, flagged here for the silent-mutation reliability angle.)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes for unsubscribe (config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) wired to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates server state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` on every request. Since this is a GET endpoint with no confirmation/CSRF protection shown, automated link fetchers (email scanners/prefetch) can trigger a silent subscription state change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id) has no rejection handler, so a failed topic load leaves the route in the generic Ember error state with the email-promised unsubscribe page never rendered. A transient load failure converts the one-shot unsubscribe link click into an unexplained error page with no retry guidance.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `topic-unsubscribe` route, `model(params)` returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no `catch`/rejection handling and no `error` action in `actions`. If the promise rejects (network/server issue), Ember will transition into its generic error state for the route, so the intended unsubscribe page/template won’t render and the user will see a generic error flow. This is a diff-grounded edge-case/UX robustness concern rather than a deterministically broken behavior shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The unsubscribe routes are not constrained to numeric topic_id on the slug variant consistently and the :summary route lost its post_number constraint in this reorder, changing match behavior for URLs like /t/slug/1/summary. Previously-rejected URLs now match :summary with post_number as part of topic_id constraints, silently rerouting malformed links.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both new unsubscribe routes are constrained to numeric `:topic_id` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" ... constraints: { topic_id: /\d+/ }` and the non-slug variant also has the same constraint), so the claim about inconsistent numeric constraints is not supported. While the `:summary` route constraints were changed (the old `post_number` constraint was removed), `post_number` is not part of the `.../:topic_id/summary` path in either version, so the finding’s stated change in URL match behavior (e.g., malformed links being newly accepted due to `post_number` becoming part of `topic_id` matching) is not verifiable from this diff and appears to misinterpret how the route is defined.
